seo_description: Free, open-source menu bar app that shows your Mac's thermal state and sensor temperatures, and notifies you when it starts to throttle. Native, offline, macOS 14+.
hero_sub: ThermalThrottleWatch lives in your menu bar and shows the system thermal state and sensor temperatures at a glance. Click the thermometer for details, and get a notification when throttling begins.
features_sub: Is your Mac under thermal stress right now? Everything here exists to answer that, read-only and on-device.

features.title: Live sensor temperatures
features.desc: See current and peak values for CPU, GPU, memory, SSD, battery and ambient sensors. Only sensors that return a plausible reading on your Mac are listed.

features.title: Thermal state in the menu bar
features.desc: A thermometer icon is tinted by the system state: Nominal, Fair, Serious or Critical. Optionally show the hottest sensor's temperature beside it.

features.title: Alerts for throttling and recovery
features.desc: Get notified when the state reaches Serious or the hottest sensor passes your threshold (60 to 105 °C). A second notification tells you when it has cooled down.

features.title: 30-minute trend and event log
features.desc: A sparkline tracks the hottest sensor, and each throttle episode is logged with its start time and duration for 14 days.

features.title: Calm, tunable alerts
features.desc: Readings are smoothed, recovery needs a 3 °C drop, and the same condition notifies at most once every 5 minutes. Choose Celsius or Fahrenheit and a 2, 5 or 10 second refresh.

features.title: Read-only and private
features.desc: No fan control, no accounts, no servers and no analytics. If sensors cannot be read, it falls back to the system thermal state and tells you so.

permissions_step: Allow notifications when prompted (or in System Settings → Notifications) so alerts can reach you; no other permissions are needed.

faq.q: Is ThermalThrottleWatch really free and open source?
faq.a: Yes. It is released under the MIT license, with no ads, accounts or paywalls. The full source is on GitHub, and you can support development with the optional Support button.
Only notifications, so it can warn you about throttling and recovery. Launch at login is optional, and it never asks for Accessibility, Screen Recording, Microphone, Camera or Location.
On your Mac only. Settings are saved in app preferences, and the 14-day throttle event log is a JSON file in Application Support. Nothing is sent anywhere.
Notarization requires a paid Apple Developer account, which this free project doesn't have. Right-click the app and choose Open once to approve it, or build it from source with Xcode.
